thread:
eva: Heads-up - NVD just published CVE-2026-32456 for lz4 v1.9.3. Decompression OOB can lead to code execution when parsing crafted frames. PoC floating on GH. https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-32456 :eyes:
raj: thanks. any EPSS/active exploit signal yet?
security-bot: EPSS: 0.42 (24h feed). Public PoC repo detected, exploit chatter on infra forum.
olivia: tagging infra owners - where do we vendor lz4? third_party or system lib?
eva: we bundle lz4 v1.9.3 in docker/image-encoder (third_party/lz4) and use system package in model-serving nodes (ubuntu 22.04 apt lz4 1.9.3). Also referenced in data-ingest microservice (python binding).
dennis: quick score: CVSS v3.1 8.7 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H). Given PoC + public exploit chatter, I'd leaning P0/P1.
raj: impact matrix: image-encoder (signs user-uploaded images) => high risk for malicious payloads. model-serving uses lz4 for cache blobs - if attacker can upload cache entries maybe remote code. data-ingest is less exposed (internal auth) but still in scope.
eva: recommended immediate actions: 1) block outbound installs of vulnerable pkg in CI; 2) patch images to lz4 1.9.6 (upstream fixed) or apply vendor backport; 3) add runtime mitigations (seccomp, restrict file perms); 4) add canary deploy for live services.
olivia: I can push a CI gate to fail builds using lz4<=1.9.3 and trigger image rebuilds. For package upgrades we need coord with distro team for apt packages.
raj: also: increase audit logging for any lz4 decompression errors. Add S3/object ingress hooks so uploads that trigger decompression get flagged. Who owns that? @olivia
olivia: I'll add an observability alert linking to a new log group and a dashboard. Need the exact error signature—anyone captured the PoC logs?
eva: PoC shows a specific mmap failure + invalid frame length. Snippet: ```error: lz4_decompress: frame_len 0xdeadbeef > input_size``` Use that regex to match.
dennis: KMS/signing question: do we verify signed artifacts for any of the ingest paths? If we rely on signed blobs (KMS-backed signatures) we can reject unsigned frames earlier.
eva: we don't currently sign uploads at upload time. Only container images are signed via build attestations stored in internal artifact registry (signed with KMS key devops-build-key). For user uploads we don't sign.
raj: short-term mitigation: restrict who can upload to public buckets and add server-side validation to reject frames with weird lengths. Also add a WAF rule to block known exploit payloads.
olivia: RBAC action: I'll create a short-lived permission change restricting S3 PutObject for unauthenticated principals and add an ACL for ingestion-lambda to only trusted roles. Will document in changelog and trigger audit log capture.
dennis: plan of record: (1) urgent patch + image rebuild - timeline 24h; (2) CI block + distro coord - 48h; (3) runtime mitigations (seccomp + input validation) - 72h; (4) RBAC hardening + audit logging - 48h; (5) postmortem + retro if exploit seen.
eva: assigning owners: image-encoder -> @dennis; model-serving -> @raj; data-ingest -> @olivia; followups in #incidents if we detect active exploitation.
security-bot: Action created: SEC-1719 (patch-and-rollout) assigned to dennis, due 2026-03-21.
raj: can someone check if any Dedicated clusters run older system lz4 libs (we have some baremetal regions)? I can run inventory sweep.
olivia: will also check KMS key usage for artifact signing and whether any ingestion paths can be retrofitted with signatures. If we can gate by signed claims, abraxa (longer-term) risk goes down.
eva: OK. For triage doc: I'll mark initial severity High, EPSS medium-high, recommended P1, and start a short Slack incident if we see exploit attempts. Please add any other quick wins to the thread. :lock: :mag:
